rows.title: On-Board Charger Failure or Charge Interruption
rows.howToFix: Diagnosis involves confirming mains supply quality, inspecting the integrated charge cable and plug for heat damage, checking the charge inlet and wiring for corrosion, and scanning Renault-specific EV modules for charger faults. Repairs range from cleaning connections or replacing the charge cable components to replacing the on-board charger assembly; minor fixes may cost $150-$400, while charger replacement can run roughly $1,000-$2,500 depending on parts source and labor.

rows.title: Battery Capacity Degradation
rows.howToFix: Monitor battery health via the Renault Z.E. app or OBD diagnostic tool. Avoid frequent rapid charging and keep charge between 20-80% for daily use. Battery lease customers can request replacement when capacity drops below 75%.

rows.title: Charging System Failure
rows.howToFix: Clean the charging port connector pins. Check for software updates to the Chameleon charger module. Replace the on-board charger unit if it consistently overheats or refuses to charge.
